macros.name: xintApplyInline
macros.doc: \xintApplyInline{\macro}{ ⟨list⟩ } works non expandably. It applies the one-parameter \macro to the first element of the expanded list (\macro may have itself some arguments, the list item will be appended as last argument), and is then re-inserted in the input stream after the tokens resulting from this first expansion of \macro.

macros.name: xintApplyUnbraced
macros.doc: \xintApplyUnbraced{\macro}{ ⟨list⟩ } is like \xintApply. The difference is that after having expanded its list argument, and applied \macro in turn to each item from the list, it reassembles the outputs without enclosing them in braces.

macros.name: xintAssign
macros.doc: \xintAssign ⟨braced things⟩ \to ⟨as many cs as they are things⟩ defines (without checking if something gets overwritten) the control sequences on the right of \to to expand to the successive tokens or braced items located to the left of \to.

macros.name: xintAssign
macros.doc: \xintAssign ⟨braced things⟩ \to ⟨as many cs as they are things⟩ defines (without checking if something gets overwritten) the control sequences on the right of \to to expand to the successive tokens or braced items located to the left of \to.

macros.name: xintBreakFor
macros.doc: One may immediately terminate an \xintFor or \xintFor* loop with \xintBreakFor.

macros.name: xintbreakiloop
macros.doc: One has \xintbreakiloop and \xintbreakiloopanddo to abort the loop.

macros.name: xintbreakloop
macros.doc: One can abort the loop with \xintbreakloop; this should not be used inside the final test, and one should expand the \fi from the corresponding test before.

macros.name: xintCSVtoList
macros.doc: \xintCSVtoList takes on input a `comma separated list of items' and converts it into a `TeX list of braced items'.

macros.name: xintifForFirst
macros.doc: \xintifForFirst {YES branch}{NO branch} and \xintifForLast {YES branch}{NO branch} execute the YES or NO branch if the \xintFor or \xintFor* loop is currently in its first, respectively last, iteration.

macros.name: xintifForLast
macros.doc: \xintifForFirst {YES branch}{NO branch} and \xintifForLast {YES branch}{NO branch} execute the YES or NO branch if the \xintFor or \xintFor* loop is currently in its first, respectively last, iteration.

macros.name: xintiloop
macros.doc: The cousin \xintiloop is \xintloop with an embedded expandable mechanism allowing to exit from the loop.

macros.name: xintiloop
macros.doc: The cousin \xintiloop is \xintloop with an embedded expandable mechanism allowing to exit from the loop.

macros.name: xintKeep
macros.doc: \xintKeep{x}{ ⟨list⟩ } expands the token list argument L and produces a new list, depending on the value of x: • if x>0, the new list contains the first x items from L (counting starts at one.)

macros.name: xintKeepNoExpand
macros.doc: \xintKeepNoExpand does not expand the L argument.

macros.name: xintKeepUnbraced
macros.doc: \xintKeepUnbraced Same as \xintKeep but no brace pairs are added around the kept items from the head of the list in the case x>0: each such item will lose one level of braces.

macros.name: xintNthElt
macros.doc: \xintNthElt{x}{ ⟨list⟩ } gets (expandably) the xth item of the ⟨list⟩ .

macros.name: xintNthEltNoExpand
macros.doc: The \xintNthEltNoExpand does no expansion of its second argument.

macros.name: xintNthOnePy
macros.doc: \xintNthOnePy{x}{ ⟨list⟩ } gets (expandably) the xth item of the ⟨list⟩ , adding a brace pair if there wasn't one.

macros.name: xintouteriloopindex
macros.doc: In case of nesting, \xintouteriloopindex gives access to the index of the outer loop.

macros.name: xintrationals
macros.doc: If the list argument to \xintFor (or \xintFor*) is \xintrationals or more generally \xintrationals[start+delta] (within braces!), then \xintFor does an infinite iteration where #1 (or #2, . . . , #9) will run through the arithmetic sequence of xintfrac fractions with initial value start and increment delta (default values: start=1/1, delta=1/1).

macros.name: xintrationals
macros.doc: If the list argument to \xintFor (or \xintFor*) is \xintrationals or more generally \xintrationals[start+delta] (within braces!), then \xintFor does an infinite iteration where #1 (or #2, . . . , #9) will run through the arithmetic sequence of xintfrac fractions with initial value start and increment delta (default values: start=1/1, delta=1/1).

macros.name: xintRelaxArray
macros.doc: \xintRelaxArray\myArray (globally) sets to \relax all macros which were defined by the previous \xintAssignArray with \myArray as array macro.

macros.name: xintRevWithBraces
macros.doc: \xintRevWithBraces{ ⟨list⟩ } first does the f -expansion of its argument then it reverses the order of the tokens, or braced material, it encounters, maintaining existing braces and adding a brace pair around each naked token encountered.

macros.name: xintSeq
macros.doc: \xintSeq[d]{x}{y} generates expandably {x}{x+d}... up to and possibly including {y} if d>0 or down to and including {y} if d<0.

macros.name: xintSeq
macros.doc: \xintSeq[d]{x}{y} generates expandably {x}{x+d}... up to and possibly including {y} if d>0 or down to and including {y} if d<0.

macros.name: xintTrimUnbraced
macros.doc: \xintTrimUnbraced Same as \xintTrim but in case of a negative x (cutting items from the tail), the kept items from the head are not enclosed in brace pairs.

macros.name: xintZapLastSpaces
macros.doc: \xintZapLastSpaces{ ⟨stuff⟩ } does not do any expansion of its argument, nor brace removal of any sort, nor does it alter ⟨stuff⟩ in anyway apart from stripping away all ending spaces.

macros.name: xintZapSpaces
macros.doc: \xintZapSpaces{ ⟨stuff⟩ } does not do any expansion of its argument, nor brace removal of any sort, nor does it alter ⟨stuff⟩ in anyway apart from stripping away all leading and all ending spaces.

macros.name: xintZapSpacesB
macros.doc: \xintZapSpacesB{ ⟨stuff⟩ } does not do any expansion of its argument, nor does it alter ⟨stuff⟩ in anyway apart from stripping away all leading and all ending spaces and possibly removing one level of braces if ⟨stuff⟩ had the shape <spaces>{braced}<spaces>.
